Stopwatch final class

Count-up stopwatch. Mirror of Timer: starts at zero, increments elapsed by $interval every tick. No upper bound. view() formats elapsed time the same way as Timer. Ticks carry the owning id and the generation epoch; update() refuses ticks addressed to other widgets or to stopped generations (M12).

MethodSummary
static setClock(?\Closure $clock): void
static new(float $interval = 1.0): self
init(): ?\Closure
update(Msg $msg): array
view(): string
stateLabel(): stringPlain-text state tag — '' while running (byte-identical running frames), 'not started' at zero, 'paused' once elapsed time is held (W-19/021 four-state matrix; see Timer::stateLabel()).
start(): arrayIdempotent — calling start() while the stopwatch is already running is a no-op so duplicate start events don't spawn parallel tick chains and double-count elapsed time. Each flip into running bumps the epoch, so a tick still in flight from a stopped generation can never count toward the restarted chain (M12).
stop(): self
reset(): self
toggle(): arrayFlip the running state. When running → stop; when stopped → start (returning the start cmd).

elapsed(): floatElapsed seconds measured against the WALL CLOCK (W-37, replaces the old tick-count accumulator): while running, the frozen base plus the real time since $resumedAt; frozen otherwise. Ticks are pure repaint drivers — a stalled loop keeps accruing real seconds while running, and start/stop transitions are the only thing that moves the base. Mirrors charmbracelet/bubbles stopwatch, which adds real message-time deltas.
interval(): floatTick cadence in seconds. Mirrors charmbracelet/bubbles Interval field which Bubbles exposes for inspection by surrounding code.

withPageSize(int $size): selfSet the number of rows displayed per page. When > 0, the table is paginated and only rows for the current page are visible. When 0 (the default), all rows are shown (no pagination). The painted window never exceeds the height set via withSize() — with both set, effectively min(pageSize, height) rows render (page advance stays pageSize-sized); height 0 means auto/unbounded, so pageSize rules.

pageLast(): selfMove the cursor to the LAST row of the visible list (GotoEnd).
nextPage(): selfAdvance to the next page. No-op when already on the last page or when pagination is disabled.
prevPage(): selfGo to the previous page. No-op when already on the first page or when pagination is disabled.

Tabs final class

A tabbed panel component — switch between labelled tabs with keyboard or mouse input.

MethodSummary
init(): ?\ClosureBubble-Tea Init — Tabs has no background commands.
static new(array $labels = [], int $width = 0): self
static interactive(array $labels, Manager|Mark $zones, int $width = 0): selfA bar ready for pointer input: new() with its zones attached.
update(Msg $msg): arrayKeyboard input is handled only while focused. Zone clicks (MsgZoneInBounds) are handled whether or not the bar is focused, and never grant focus. The Cmd is non-null only when a tab was closed; it yields a TabClosedMsg.
view(): stringRender the tab bar as a single line.
spans(): arrayThe cells each visible tab occupies on the frame view() draws, in display order — the hit-testing surface for hosts that route clicks by column instead of by zone markup.
tabAt(int $col): ?intThe visible tab under bar column $col, or null (a divider, a scroll mark, or past the end).
clickAt(int $col): arrayApply a click at bar column $col (0-based, relative to the bar's first cell): a click on a tab activates it, a click on a closable tab's close affordance closes it. Not focus-gated.
clickZone(string $zoneId): arrayApply a click on the zone named $zoneId — the id exactly as it appears in the frame (with the Manager prefix on a Manager bar, bare on a Mark bar). Ids minted by another bar, or naming a tab outside the visible window, leave the bar unchanged. Not focus-gated.
active(): intCurrently active tab index (0-based).
labels(): array
badge(int $index): ?stringBadge text of tab $index, or null when the tab carries none.
withLabels(array $labels): self
withBadge(int $index, ?string $badge): selfSet the badge of tab $index (an unread count, a !, a dirty dot), rendered after the label. Null or the empty string removes it. Badge text is sanitized like labels, so it cannot forge zone markup.
withBadgeStyle(?Style $style): selfStyle for badges; null (the default) draws a badge in its tab's style.
withClosable(bool $closable = true): selfMake every tab closable: each tab draws a close affordance after its label (and badge), a click on it closes the tab, and the keymap's closeTab binding (ctrl+w) closes the active tab while focused. Each close returns a Cmd carrying TabClosedMsg.
withCloseGlyph(string $glyph): selfReplace the close-affordance glyph (default CLOSE_GLYPH).
withPlaceholder(string $text): selfText view() renders when the bar has no tabs (in the inactive style, clipped to the width). The empty string, the default, renders nothing. Sanitized like labels.
moveTab(int $from, int $to): selfMove tab $from to position $to; the tabs between shift by one. The tab keeps its badge, and the active tab stays the same tab (its index follows the move). The scroll window follows the active tab.
closeTab(int $index): selfRemove tab $index. Later tabs shift left with their badges. When the active tab closes, its right-hand neighbor becomes active (the left one when it was the last tab); closing another tab keeps the same tab active. Closing the only tab leaves an empty bar.
withActive(int $index): selfActivate tab $index. Out-of-range indices are a programming error, not a style choice: typed throw naming the grammar-free range (the tabs.bad_index the vocabulary promised). An empty tab list has no selection to move — $this is returned. The constructor carries the same guard; render-time clamping stays as a defensive belt for hand-built instances, not a substitute for setter enforcement.
withActiveStyle(Style $style): self
withInactiveStyle(Style $style): self
withDivider(string $divider): self
withKeyMap(TabsKeyMap $keyMap): self
withWidth(int $width): self
withZoneManager(?Manager $manager): selfAttach a Manager for mouse-click zone tracking.
withMark(?Mark $mark): selfAttach a manager-free Mark so view() publishes zone markers without a Manager: each visible tab is wrapped in <zoneKey>tab-N (and <zoneKey>close-N around a close affordance), unprefixed. The host scans the frame (a sugar-mouse Scanner) and passes the hit zone's id to clickZone(). A Manager, when also attached, takes precedence. Null detaches.
withZoneKey(string $key): selfPin this bar's zone key (the per-bar prefix of its tab zone ids).
withLabelPadding(int $left, int $right): selfSet the blank cells drawn on each side of every label (default 1 and 1: Home ). withLabelPadding(0, 0) draws the bare label, for a host that frames its tabs itself. Only the label is padded: a badge and the close affordance keep their own trailing cell. Spans, tabAt(), clickAt() and the scroll window measure the padded text, so hit-tests stay on the drawn cells for any padding.
withDividerStyle(?Style $style): selfStyle the divider text between tabs (and a divider the width clips). Null, the default, draws it in the inactive tab style.
withScrollMarks(string $left, string $right, ?Style $markStyle = null, bool $separatorAfterLeft = true): selfSet the marks drawn when tabs are scrolled off each side of a width-bounded bar, and the style they are drawn in. The right mark is also the one an overflowing line ends with once it is clipped. The defaults (SCROLL_MARK on both sides, no style, a divider after the left mark) are the bar's frame without this call. $separatorAfterLeft = false draws the first visible tab right after the left mark, with no divider between them; the right mark keeps its divider. Marks are sanitized like labels; the scroll window, spans() and the hit-tests price them at their drawn width, and the window scrolls to keep the active tab in view under the new widths.
withScrollWindow(ScrollWindow $mode): selfPick how the scroll window follows the active tab: ScrollWindow::Offset (the default) keeps the stored offset and slides it by the least that reveals the active tab; ScrollWindow::FirstKeepingActive scans from the first tab and shows the first run of tabs that keeps the active tab in view, and ignores withScrollOffset().
withScrollOffset(int $offset): selfManually set the scroll offset (first visible tab index), clamped to the tab list. Auto-scroll that keeps the active tab visible is driven internally by update() — this setter pins an explicit offset. Under ScrollWindow::FirstKeepingActive the active tab alone decides the window, so the pinned offset is not used.
noWrap(): selfDisable wrap-around at the ends of the tab list. With wrap disabled, Tab clamps at the last tab and Shift+Tab clamps at the first tab.
focus(): selfTake focus; companion to blur() — a pure value verb.
blur(): self

Timer final class

Countdown timer. Construct with a duration; call start() to begin ticking. update() consumes TimerTicks and reschedules the next tick until $remaining hits zero, at which point a single TimeoutMsg is dispatched and the timer stops itself.

MethodSummary
static new(float $duration, float $interval = 1.0): self
init(): ?\Closure
update(Msg $msg): array
view(): string
stateLabel(): stringPlain-text state tag for the non-running states — '' while running, so the running bytes stay byte-identical (hard constraint). Timeout and pause were invisible in the frame: a paused '0:10' and a fresh '0:10', or a timed-out '0:00' and a reset '0:00', rendered the same, leaving AT consumers nothing to diff (W-19/021). Hosts that want to style the tag themselves compose it from this label.
start(): arraySet running=true and schedule the first tick. Idempotent — calling start() while the timer is already running is a no-op so duplicate start events don't spawn parallel tick chains. Each flip into running bumps the epoch, so a tick still in flight from a stopped generation can never count toward the restarted chain (M12).
stop(): self
reset(?float $duration = null): selfReset to a new duration (or the current one) and stop.
toggle(): arrayFlip the running state. When running → stop; when stopped → start (returning the start cmd).
isRunning(): bool
timedOut(): bool
id(): intStable per-instance ID — used by TimerTick / TimeoutMsg routing. Mirrors charmbracelet/bubbles ID().
interval(): floatTick cadence in seconds. Mirrors charmbracelet/bubbles Interval field which Bubbles exposes for inspection by surrounding code (e.g. progress bars syncing animation frames to the tick interval).
timeout(): floatRemaining duration in seconds. Mirrors charmbracelet/bubbles Timeout field. Returns 0 for a timer that has fired its TimeoutMsg; returns the original duration before start() is called.
withInterval(float $interval): selfRecreate the timer with a new interval. Stopped/running state and the remaining duration are preserved. Mirrors charmbracelet/bubbles' mutable Interval field assignment (which we render immutable here so snapshot-based tests stay deterministic).
static format(float $seconds): stringFormat seconds as "H:MM:SS" / "M:SS" / "0:SS" depending on magnitude. Non-finite input and negative durations render the sane zero state ('0:00'), matching the NaN-clamps-to-empty posture the percent ladder holds — a public static, so it is QA-visible surface (M63; the consistent '-0:05' spelling stays the gated alternative).
